Method of Attack: Exposes a localhost NodeJS server endpoint that executes arbitrary JavaScript code from JSON POST requests in a sandboxed environment using node:vm module
Sandbox escape via bypasses in the safe-eval style sandbox allowing arbitrary code execution
Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) vulnerability allowing any website to trigger code execution via crafted POST requests bypassing CORS restrictions
Exploitation leads to Remote Code Execution (RCE) on the developer's local machine
Impacted Systems: NodeJS servers running @nestjs/devtools-integration on localhost during development
Attack Vector: Malicious website triggers CSRF POST requests with crafted payloads to localhost endpoints
Sandbox escape payloads executed via the vulnerable sandboxedCodeExecutor
Bypassing CORS via text/plain content-type POST requests and form submissions
Indicators of Compromise: Requests to http://localhost:8000/inspector/graph/interact with JSON payload containing 'code' field
Use of payloads like (function() { try{ propertyIsEnumerable.call(); } catch(pp){ pp.constructor.constructor('return process')().mainModule.require('child_process').execSync(...) } })()
Presence of Access-Control-Allow-Origin header set to https://devtools.nestjs.com but ineffective due to CSRF
Use of safe-eval style sandboxing with vm.runInNewContext and disabling Function constructor
Date of Discovery: 2023-2024 timeframe (exact date not specified, advisory GHSA-85cg-cmq5-qjm7 and CVE-2025-54782)
Version: vulnerable versions locked in dependency (exact version not specified)
